newsitem.title: JAMAICA: Jamaica denies knowledge of officials' drug links.
newsitem.headline: Jamaica denies knowledge of officials' drug links.

text.p: The government on Tuesday dismissed allegations by a senior U.S. official that Jamaican politicians had ties to drug barons.

National Security Minister K.D. Knight said in a statement: "The Jamaican government is not aware of any names of elected government representatives suspected of such activities. (We) would expect that any such information would be made available to the commissioner of police for appropriate action."

Knight said the U.S. Drug Enforcement Agency regularly shared names with local police in Jamaica, who have been told "the law must take its course regardless of political affiliation." He said the government planned to file a formal request with U.S. authorities for information that would lead to the arrest of any politician with criminal links.

Patricia Hall, the U.S. State Department's director for Latin American and Caribbean drug enforcement programmes, said on Monday that Washington was aware of at least one elected representative who had regular contact with drug barons. She said the Jamaican government knew who the people were but refused to move against them, either out of fear of reprisals or because "the pool may be deeper than it appears."
Hall, speaking from Washington in a satellite press conference with Jamaica and Trinidad, said Washington was considering slashing aid to Jamaica because of its lack of progress in the drug war.
U.S. officials estimate 35 percent of cocaine produced in South America is shipped through the Caribbean. Jamaica tops the list of the largest exporters of marijuana in the region.
